title: temporal-shot-scheduler-notes
content:
Notes to self - temporal few-shot scheduling experiments

High-level idea (sketch):
- Rather than stuffing k examples at the front of the context window, treat the context as a timeline and place a mix of older + very recent shots distributed across the window. Hypothesis: recency helps with factual freshness, diversity across window helps calibration and reduces priming drift.
- Call this: temporal-shot-scheduler (TSS). Scheduler decides: which examples, how many tokens between them, and whether to include inline meta (source/date).

Why this feels promising (intuition):
- Large contexts have local attention biases: tokens closer to current prompt can dominate. If we want the model to consider both stable schema-like patterns (older canonical examples) and recent user-specific examples, scattering might maintain influence of both.
- Experimentally some models overweight earliest examples; some overweight latest. TSS can adapt schedule per-model profile.

Design notes / variables to sweep:
- spacing pattern: clustered (all shots at start), even spacing, exponentially decaying spacing (more shots near prompt), reverse (more older shots nearer prompt).
- meta tags: add [DATE: YYYY-MM-DD], [SOURCE: support-ticket], or omit. Test with/without.
- shot types: positive example (good answer), contrastive negative (bad answer), neutral template. Mix ratios (e.g., 3:1:1).
- shot length budget constraints: keep total examples tokens <= 30% of context. Also test token-limited vs example-limited.
- model target: run on gpt-style open LLMs we host + one open small model baseline. Track differences.

Initial prompt skeleton (prototype):
--- system/context header ---
You are an assistant that follows examples. When questions are ambiguous, prefer concise factual answers.

--- temporal shots (scheduler output) ---
[EXAMPLE 1 | DATE: 2024-08-03 | TYPE: positive]
Q: How do I rotate keys in the KMS?
A: Use the rotate-key endpoint with the following steps: 1) request new key 2) re-encrypt artifacts 3) update alias. Keep alias stable during swap.

[EXAMPLE 2 | DATE: 2025-01-17 | TYPE: positive]
Q: My inference latency spikes when memory fills. What to check?
A: Inspect KV cache size, batching config, and model quantization mismatches. Consider enabling auto-batching and reducing max_new_tokens.

... (more shots spaced according to schedule)

--- user question ---
Q: How can I rotate keys during a zero-downtime deployment?
A:

Observation: shots with explicit DATE increased model tendency to prefer the most recent pattern for procedural steps, but sometimes it over-applies very recent but domain-irrelevant phrasing. Need heuristics to filter by 'domain similarity' score.

Metrics to record per run:
- instruction-following score (rubric-based, 0-1)
- hallucination rate (binary per answer, manual/automatic detect)
- concise-ness (tokens in answer)
- latency overhead (ms) from increased context size
- token-cost delta ($)
- calibration drift: how much the answer style shifts when schedule changes (qualitative tag set)

Planned experiments (short roadmap):
1) Small sweep (50 prompts): spacing pattern (clustered / even / exponential) x 3 shot budgets (3/5/8) on two models. Quick manual eval. (Timeline: 1 week)
2) Add date/meta ablation: with date, without date, with domain tag. Measure misc.
3) Automatic scheduling rules: naive scoring of candidate shots by similarity to query (embedding cosine), then interleave top-K at positions determined by pattern. Compare to random selection.
4) Deploy an online A/B on a small internal flow (helpdesk reply suggestion) to measure CTR on accepted suggestions. (Needs privacy review).

Failure cases logged so far (notes):
- Example bleed: when an old negative example is placed too near the end, model copies the wrong phrasing exactly. (Mitigation: add explicit "Do not follow the bad example" clause at end of prompt or use contrast markers.)
- Style drift: scattered shots sometimes create mixed register responses (formal + casual). Consider uniformizing style in all examples or add style constraint at top.
- Cost blowup: even spacing with many long examples increases tokens drastically; need heuristic to truncate examples by keeping only the minimal rationalization tokens.
- Overfitting to dates: model picks date-specific content even when irrelevant. Option: only include relative time tags ("2 weeks ago") or domain-limited timestamps.

Quick heuristics & rules I want to test: 
- Limit total example tokens to 25% of context for latency-sensitive flows.
- For retrieval-augmented shots, always place the freshest retrieved item within the last 512 tokens.
- If similarity score < 0.45, place the shot further from the prompt (to lower influence).
- If shot is labeled 'negative', always place it >1024 tokens away unless explicit contrast teaching is required.

Mini experiments run 2025-01 (results, rough):
- Even spacing + date tags improved accuracy in 7/10 prompts vs clustered baseline for model-A.
- Model-B (smaller) ignored spacing; it only used the two closest examples. So per-model scheduler profiles needed.
- Negative-example placement: when negative placed middle, model sometimes reproduces errors; placing negative earliest (left-most) reduces copying but increases confusion (it treats some negatives as canonical unless flagged).

To-dos / next steps (short):
- Implement scheduler prototype that takes: candidate_shots[], query_embedding, model_profile -> arranged_prompt. (Ticket: MLINFRA-211)
- Build quick eval harness to compute instruction-following metric (semi-automated; need 50 labelled examples).
- Talk to Solutions Eng (Ethan) about trying in a small customer demo for release notes summarization.
- Draft an internal short note on risks (cost, privacy) before any live test.

Rough idea for API call shape:
POST /v1/prompt_scheduler/arrange
body: {"query": "...", "candidates": [{"text":"...","date":"2024-11-01","domain":"billing"}, ...], "pattern":"exponential", "max_example_tokens": 2048, "model":"rwi-ggml-13b"}
response: {"arranged_prompt": "<text>", "positions": [256, 1024, ...], "estimated_tokens": 3200}

Random notes:
- Keep record of which examples actually influenced the output (use saliency/token-attribution trick from the runtime) — useful to prune.
- Might be worth combining with Redwood Optimize signals (batching/quantization) to recommend how many tokens we can safely add for a given latency SLO.

End of scratchpad.

Unresolved questions (for later):
- How does temporal scattering interact with model-specific attention patterns (rotary vs ALiBi)? Need collaboration with infra/serving-runtime to map kernel-level behavior to high-level scheduling.
- Does adding explicit "do not imitate negative examples" instruction reduce utility of negatives? tradeoffs?

Notes to self: keep this doc ephemeral. Move polished experimental results into a shared drive doc if promising.
